Report
(1) The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) must prepare a report in relation to the Regional Broadband Scheme that includes:
the estimates referred to in subsection (3); and
such other matters (if any) as the ACCC considers relevant.

The purpose of the report is to provide updated costings in relation to the amount of the base component specified in paragraph 12(1)(a) of the Regional Broadband Scheme Charge Act, using the same model and methodology that was previously used to determine that amount but taking into account changes to inputs and assumptions that have occurred since that amount was first determined.
The report must include an estimate of each of the following:
the total losses that have been incurred by NBN Co in relation to fixed wireless broadband and satellite broadband matters during the period beginning on 1 July 2009 and ending on 30 June 2020;

(b) the total of the reasonable losses likely to be incurred by NBN Co in relation to fixed wireless broadband and satellite broadband matters during the period beginning on 1 July 2009 and ending on 30 June 2040 (the total expected net losses);

the amount that the base component for a month (within the meaning of the Regional Broadband Scheme Charge Act) would be required to be in order for the Commonwealth to receive a total amount by way of charge imposed by that Act that would offset the total expected net losses, if it were assumed that paragraph 9(1)(b) of that Act had not been enacted;

(d) the total of the reasonable losses likely to be incurred by NBN Co in relation to fixed wireless broadband and satellite broadband matters during the period beginning on 1 July 2020 and ending on 30 June 2040 (the total expected net forward facing losses);

the amount that the base component for a month (within the meaning of the Regional Broadband Scheme Charge Act) would be required to be in order for the Commonwealth to receive a total amount by way of charge imposed by that Act that would offset the total expected net forward facing losses, if it were assumed that paragraph 9(1)(b) of that Act had not been enacted;
the total expected number of chargeable premises by reference to which charge is to be calculated under the Regional Broadband Scheme Charge Act during the financial year beginning on 1 July 2025;
such other matters (if any) as the ACCC considers relevant.
Note: For paragraph (f), see section 11 of the Regional Broadband Scheme Charge Act in relation to how numbers of chargeable premises are used in calculating charge under that Act.
The report must specify the aggregated data inputs and the modelling assumptions upon which the estimates referred to in subsection (3) were determined.
In preparing the report, the ACCC:

(a) must use the methodology and model that was used by the Department of Communications and the Arts’ Bureau of Communications Research for the report entitled NBN non-commercial services funding options—Final report March 2016; but
must, in doing so, update the inputs and assumptions of the methodology and model to reflect changes that have occurred since the publication of that report.
Without limiting paragraph (5)(b), the following are changes that must be taken into account in updating the inputs and assumptions:
changes in the inputs for estimating the total number of chargeable premises by reference to which charge is imposed by the Regional Broadband Scheme Charge Act;
changes in the inputs for build costs in relation to fixed wireless broadband and satellite broadband matters;
changes in the inputs for estimating future capital expenditure requirements in relation to fixed wireless broadband and satellite broadband matters.
(7) In preparing the report, the ACCC must assume that Division 6 of Part 3 of the Telecommunications (Consumer Protection and Service Standards) Act 1999 had not been enacted.
Note: That Division deals with charge offset certificates.
Before the end of the 150-day period beginning when this section commences, the ACCC must:
give the Minister the report; and
make the report available on the ACCC’s website.
The Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 5 sitting days of receiving it.

section.heading: Compliance with conditions and limitations of exemption determinations

content.p: A person must, on or after the designated commencement date, comply with the conditions or limitations of a determination under subsection 143A(1) or (2).

A person must not:
aid, abet, counsel or procure a contravention of subsection (1); or
induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a contravention of subsection (1); or
be in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, a contravention of subsection (1); or
conspire with others to effect a contravention of subsection (1).

(3) Subsections (1) and (2) are civil penalty provisions.

section.heading: Judicial enforcement of conditions and limitations of exemption determinations

content.p: If the Federal Court is satisfied that a person has, on or after the designated commencement date, contravened any of the conditions or limitations of a determination under subsection 143A(1) or (2), the Court may, on the application of:
the ACCC; or
a carrier; or
a carriage service provider;

an order directing the person to comply with the condition or limitation;
an order directing the person to compensate any other person (who may be the applicant) who has suffered loss or damage as a result of the contravention;
any other order that the Court thinks appropriate.
The Federal Court may discharge or vary an order granted under this section.

section.heading: Publication of list of persons who have elected to be bound by exemption determinations

content.p: If a determination is in force under subsection 143A(1) or (2), the ACCC must publish on its website a list setting out the names of the persons who:
have elected to be bound by the determination; and

the extension is for a period of not more than 3 months; and
the notice includes a statement explaining why the ACCC has been unable to make a decision on the undertaking within the initial 3-month period.
As soon as practicable after the ACCC gives a notice under subsection (7), the ACCC must publish a copy of the notice on the ACCC’s website.
Scope
This section applies if:
a person gives the ACCC a standard functional separation undertaking; or
2 or more persons give the ACCC a joint functional separation undertaking.
Consultation
Before making a decision to accept or reject the undertaking, the ACCC must:
publish on the ACCC’s website a notice:
setting out the undertaking; and
inviting persons to make submissions to the ACCC about the undertaking within the time limit specified in the notice; and
consider any submissions received within the time limit specified in the notice.
The time limit must not be shorter than 15 business days after the notice is published.
If:
(a) a person gives the ACCC a standard functional separation undertaking (the first functional separation undertaking); and
the ACCC rejects the first functional separation undertaking; and
the person subsequently gives the ACCC another standard functional separation undertaking; and

the ACCC is satisfied that any or all of the provisions of the first functional separation undertaking are materially similar to any or all of the provisions of the other functional separation undertaking;
the ACCC may refuse to consider the other functional separation undertaking.
If:
(a) 2 or more persons give the ACCC a joint functional separation undertaking (the first functional separation undertaking); and
the ACCC rejects the first functional separation undertaking; and
those persons subsequently give the ACCC another joint functional separation undertaking; and

the ACCC is satisfied that any or all of the provisions of the first functional separation undertaking are materially similar to any or all of the provisions of the other functional separation undertaking;
the ACCC may refuse to consider the other functional separation undertaking.
Refund of fee
If:
the ACCC refuses to consider a functional separation undertaking under this section; and
a person or persons have paid a fee in relation to the undertaking;
the ACCC must, on behalf of the Commonwealth, refund the fee.

section.heading: Criteria for accepting functional separation undertaking

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a person gives the ACCC a standard functional separation undertaking; or
2 or more persons give the ACCC a joint functional separation undertaking.
Criteria
In deciding whether to accept the undertaking, the ACCC must have regard to:
whether the undertaking promotes the long-term interests of end-users of carriage services or of services supplied by means of carriage services; and
the matters (if any) specified in a determination that was in force under subsection (3) at the time the undertaking was given; and
such other matters (if any) as the ACCC considers relevant.
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine one or more matters for the purposes of paragraph (2)(b).

section.heading: Variation of functional separation undertaking that is under consideration

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
(a) a person gives the ACCC a standard functional separation undertaking (the original undertaking); or
(b) 2 or more persons give the ACCC a joint functional separation undertaking (the original undertaking).
Notice
The ACCC may give the person or persons a written notice stating that, if:
the person makes, or the persons make, such variations to the original undertaking as are specified in the notice; and
the person gives, or the persons give, the varied undertaking to the ACCC within the period specified in the notice;
the ACCC will consider the varied undertaking under section 151F as if the varied undertaking had been given to the ACCC instead of the original undertaking.
Treatment of varied undertaking

If the person gives, or the persons give, the ACCC a varied undertaking in response to the notice, the ACCC must consider the varied undertaking under section 151F as if the varied undertaking had been given to the ACCC instead of the original undertaking.
No duty to consider whether to give a notice
The ACCC does not have a duty to consider whether to give a notice under subsection (2).

section.heading: Replacement of functional separation undertaking that is under consideration

content.p: Scope
(1) This section applies if a person gives the ACCC a standard functional separation undertaking (the original undertaking).
Notice
The ACCC may give the person a written notice stating that, if:
the person withdraws the original undertaking; and
the person, together with one or more other persons specified in the notice, gives a joint functional separation undertaking in the terms specified in the notice; and
the person does the things mentioned in paragraphs (a) and (b) within the time limit specified in the notice;
the ACCC would be inclined to accept the joint functional separation undertaking.
The ACCC does not have a duty to consider whether to give a notice under subsection (2).
If:
(a) a standard functional separation undertaking (the existing undertaking) given by a person is in force; and
at least 12 months before the expiry of the existing undertaking, the person gives the ACCC another standard functional separation undertaking;
the other undertaking may be expressed to be given by way of renewal of the existing undertaking.
Note: For acceptance or rejection of the other undertaking, see section 151F.
If:
(a) a joint functional separation undertaking (the existing undertaking) given by 2 or more persons is in force; and
at least 12 months before the expiry of the existing undertaking, those persons give another joint functional separation undertaking to the ACCC;
the other undertaking may be expressed to be given by way of renewal of the existing undertaking.
Note 1: For acceptance or rejection of the other undertaking, see section 151F.
Note 2: For consultation on a decision to accept or reject the other undertaking, see section 151G.

section.heading: Variation of expiry time of certain functional separation undertakings

content.p: Standard functional separation undertaking
If:
(a) a standard functional separation undertaking (the existing undertaking) given by a person is in force; and
another functional separation undertaking is given to the ACCC by the person; and
the ACCC rejects the other undertaking;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to the person, vary the existing undertaking by:
omitting the expiry time specified in the existing undertaking; and
substituting the expiry time specified in the notice.
Note: See also section 142B.
The expiry time specified in the notice:
must be later than the rejection of the other undertaking; and
must not be later than 12 months after the rejection of the other undertaking.
Subsection 151A(8) does not apply to an expiry time specified in a notice under subsection (1).
Joint functional separation undertaking
If:
(a) a joint functional separation undertaking (the existing undertaking) given by 2 or more persons is in force; and
another functional separation undertaking is given to the ACCC by a person who is one of the persons mentioned in paragraph (a); and
the ACCC rejects the other undertaking;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to each of the persons mentioned in paragraph (a), vary the existing undertaking by:
omitting the expiry time specified in the existing undertaking; and
substituting the expiry time specified in the notice.
Note: See also section 142B.
The expiry time specified in the notice:
must be later than the rejection of the other undertaking; and
must not be later than 12 months after the rejection of the other undertaking.
Subsection 151C(8) does not apply to an expiry time specified in a notice under subsection (4).
Consultation
Before making a decision under this section to vary a functional separation undertaking, the ACCC must:
publish on the ACCC’s website a notice:
setting out the proposed variation; and
inviting persons to make submissions to the ACCC about the proposed variation within the time limit specified in the notice; and
consider any submissions received within the time limit specified in the notice.
The time limit must not be shorter than 15 business days after the notice is published.
Scope
This section applies if:
either:
(i) a person gives the ACCC a standard functional separation undertaking (the new undertaking); or
(ii) 2 or more persons give the ACCC a joint functional separation undertaking (the new undertaking); and
the ACCC accepts the new undertaking.
Duration
If the new undertaking is not expressed to be given by way of renewal of another functional separation undertaking:
in a case where the new undertaking is accepted before the designated commencement date—the new undertaking comes into force:
on the designated commencement date; or
if a later day is specified in the new undertaking—on that day; and
in a case where the new undertaking is accepted on or after the designated commencement date—the new undertaking comes into force:
on the day after it is accepted; or
if a later day is specified in the new undertaking—on that day; and
unless sooner revoked, the new undertaking continues in force until it expires.
If the new undertaking is expressed to be given by way of renewal of another functional separation undertaking:
the new undertaking comes into force immediately after the expiry of the other undertaking; and
unless sooner revoked, the new undertaking continues in force until it expires.

section.heading: Variation of functional separation undertaking that is in force

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a standard functional separation undertaking given by a person is in force; or
a joint functional separation undertaking given by 2 or more persons is in force.
Variation
The person or persons may give the ACCC a variation of the undertaking.
If the undertaking is a standard functional separation undertaking, the undertaking as varied must comply with subsections 151A(2), (5), (8), (9), (10) and (11) and paragraph 151A(4)(a).
If the undertaking is a joint functional separation undertaking, the undertaking as varied must comply with subsections 151C(2), (5), (8), (9), (10), (11), (12) and (13) and paragraph 151C(4)(a).
Form etc.
The variation must:
be accompanied by such information as is reasonably likely to assist the ACCC to decide whether to accept or reject the variation; and
be accompanied by the fee (if any) specified in, or ascertained in accordance with, a determination under subsection (6).
The ACCC may, by legislative instrument, determine a fee, or a method of ascertaining a fee, for the purposes of paragraph (5)(b).
A fee determined under, or ascertained in accordance with, subsection (6) must not be such as to amount to taxation.

section.heading: Further information about variation of functional separation undertaking

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a person gives the ACCC a variation of a standard functional separation undertaking; or
2 or more persons give the ACCC a variation of a joint functional separation undertaking.
Request for further information
The ACCC may request the person or persons to give the ACCC further information about the variation.
The ACCC may refuse to consider the variation until the person or persons give the ACCC the information.
The ACCC may withdraw its request for further information, in whole or in part.

section.heading: Withdrawal of variation that is under consideration

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a person gives the ACCC a variation of a standard functional separation undertaking; or
2 or more persons give the ACCC a variation of a joint functional separation undertaking.
Withdrawal
The person or persons may withdraw the variation at any time before the ACCC makes a decision to accept or reject the variation.
This Act does not prevent the person or persons from giving a fresh variation.
Refund of fee
If:
the person or persons withdraw the variation; and
the person or persons have paid a fee in relation to the variation;
the ACCC may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, refund the whole or a part of the fee.

section.heading: ACCC to accept or reject variation

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a person gives the ACCC a variation of a standard functional separation undertaking; or
2 or more persons give the ACCC a variation of a joint functional separation undertaking.
Decision to accept or reject variation
After considering the variation, the ACCC must:
accept the variation; or
reject the variation.
Notice of decision
If the ACCC accepts the variation, the ACCC must give the person or persons a written notice:
stating that the variation has been accepted; and
setting out the terms of the variation.
If the ACCC rejects the variation, the ACCC must give the person or persons a written notice:
stating that the variation has been rejected; and
setting out the reasons for the rejection.
ACCC to make decision within 3 months
The ACCC must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision about the variation is made under subsection (2) within 3 months after receiving the variation.
In calculating the 3-month period referred to in subsection (5), disregard:
a day in the period:
beginning on the day on which the ACCC published the variation under section 151U; and
ending at the end of the time limit specified by the ACCC when it published the variation under section 151U; and
if the ACCC has requested further information under section 151R in relation to the variation—a day during any part of which the request, or any part of the request, remains unfulfilled.
Extension of decision-making period
(7) The ACCC may, by written notice given to the person or persons, extend the 3-month period referred to in subsection (5) (the initial 3-month period), so long as:
the extension is for a period of not more than 3 months; and
the notice includes a statement explaining why the ACCC has been unable to make a decision on the variation within the initial 3-month period.
As soon as practicable after the ACCC gives a notice under subsection (7), the ACCC must publish a copy of the notice on the ACCC’s website.
Scope
This section applies if:
a person gives the ACCC a variation of a standard functional separation undertaking; or
2 or more persons give the ACCC a variation of a joint functional separation undertaking.
Consultation
Before making a decision to accept or reject the variation, the ACCC must:
publish on the ACCC’s website a notice:
setting out the variation; and
inviting persons to make submissions to the ACCC about the variation within the time limit specified in the notice; and
consider any submissions received within the time limit specified in the notice.
The time limit must not be shorter than 15 business days after the notice is published.
Scope
This section applies if:
a person gives the ACCC a variation of a standard functional separation undertaking; or
2 or more persons give the ACCC a variation of a joint functional separation undertaking.
Criteria
In deciding whether to accept the variation, the ACCC must have regard to:
whether the variation promotes the long-term interests of end-users of carriage services or of services supplied by means of carriage services; and
the matters (if any) specified in a determination under subsection (3); and
such other matters (if any) as the ACCC considers relevant.
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine one or more matters for the purposes of paragraph (2)(b).
Standard functional separation undertaking
If:
a standard functional separation undertaking given by a person is in force; and
the person has:
breached a fundamental provision of the undertaking; or
contravened section 151ZF or 151ZG;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to the person, revoke the undertaking.
If:
a standard functional separation undertaking given by a person is in force; and
the ACCC is satisfied that the person has an unsatisfactory compliance record in relation to functional separation;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to the person, revoke the undertaking.
If:
a standard functional separation undertaking given by a person is in force; and
the person requests the ACCC, in writing, to revoke the undertaking;
the ACCC must, by written notice given to the person, revoke the undertaking.
A revocation under subsection (1), (2) or (3) takes effect at the time specified in the notice of revocation. The specified time:
must not be earlier than the time the notice is given; and
must not be later than 12 months after the notice is given.
After the giving of a notice of revocation of a standard functional separation undertaking under subsection (1), (2) or (3):
the undertaking does not apply to local access line services supplied using a local access line that came into existence after the notice was given; and

(b) the definitions of retail business unit and wholesale business unit in section 142A (in so far as those definitions relate to the undertaking) have effect as if references in those definitions to the supply of local access line services did not include the supply of local access line services using a local access line that came into existence after the notice was given.
Joint functional separation undertaking
If:
a joint functional separation undertaking given by 2 or more persons is in force; and
any of those persons has:
breached a fundamental provision of the undertaking; or
contravened section 151ZF or 151ZG;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to each of those persons, revoke the undertaking.
If:
a joint functional separation undertaking given by 2 or more persons is in force; and
the ACCC is satisfied that any of those persons has an unsatisfactory compliance record in relation to functional separation;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to each of those persons, revoke the undertaking.
If:
a joint functional separation undertaking given by 2 or more persons is in force; and
those persons request the ACCC, in writing, to revoke the undertaking;
the ACCC must, by written notice given to each of those persons, revoke the undertaking.
A revocation under subsection (6), (7) or (8) takes effect at the time specified in the notice of revocation. The specified time:
must not be earlier than the time the notice is given; and
must not be later than 12 months after the notice is given.

After the giving of a notice of revocation of a joint functional separation undertaking under subsection (6), (7) or (8), the undertaking does not apply to local access line services supplied using a local access line that came into existence after the notice was given.
Matters to which the ACCC must have regard
In exercising its powers under this section, the ACCC must have regard to the following matters:
whether arrangements to maintain the continuity of the supply of superfast carriage services to residential customers using local access lines:
have been made; or
can be made before the relevant revocation takes effect;
in the case of a revocation under subsection (1) or (6)—the consequences of the breach;
in the case of a revocation under subsection (2) or (7)—the consequences of the person’s unsatisfactory compliance record;
such other matters (if any) as the ACCC considers relevant.
Revocation of standard functional separation undertaking
Before making a decision under subsection 151W(1) or (2) to revoke a standard functional separation undertaking given by a person, the ACCC must:
give the person a written notice:
stating that the ACCC proposes to revoke the undertaking; and
inviting the person to make a submission to the ACCC about the revocation within the time limit specified in the notice; and
consider any submission received within the time limit specified in the notice.
The time limit must not be shorter than 15 business days after the notice is given.
Revocation of joint functional separation undertaking
Before making a decision under subsection 151W(6) or (7) to revoke a joint functional separation undertaking given by 2 or more persons, the ACCC must:
give each of those persons a written notice:
stating that the ACCC proposes to revoke the undertaking; and
inviting those persons to make submissions to the ACCC about the revocation within the time limit specified in the notice; and
consider any submissions received within the time limit specified in the notice.
The time limit must not be shorter than 15 business days after the notice is given.

section.heading: Notification that a person is at risk of having an unsatisfactory compliance record in relation to functional separation

content.p: Scope
This section applies to:
a breach by a person of a functional separation undertaking given by the person, so long as the breach occurred when the undertaking was in force; and
a contravention by a person of section 143B, 151ZA, 151ZB, 151ZF, 151ZG, 151ZH or 151ZI.
Note: See section 142B.
Notification
If:
a functional separation undertaking given by a person is in force; and
the ACCC is aware of one or more breaches or contraventions by the person; and
the ACCC is satisfied that those breaches or contraventions do not mean that the person has an unsatisfactory compliance record in relation to functional separation; and

the ACCC is satisfied that, if there were to be a particular kind of additional breach or contravention by the person, the person would have an unsatisfactory compliance record in relation to functional separation;
the ACCC must:
give the person a written notice:
stating that the ACCC considers that the person is at risk of having an unsatisfactory compliance record in relation to functional separation; and
informing the person that an unsatisfactory compliance record is a ground for revoking the undertaking; and
do so as soon as practicable after becoming satisfied as mentioned in paragraph (d).
Note: See section 142B.
A failure to comply with subsection (2) does not affect the validity of a revocation of a functional separation undertaking.

section.heading: Variation of functional separation undertaking following giving of revocation notice

content.p: Standard functional separation undertaking
If:
the ACCC has given a notice under section 151W revoking a standard functional separation undertaking; and
the revocation has not taken effect;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to the person who gave the undertaking, vary the undertaking.
The ACCC must not vary a standard functional separation undertaking under subsection (1) unless the variation:
addresses the matter or matters that constituted the grounds for the revocation of the undertaking under section 151W; and
does not address any other matter.
Joint functional separation undertaking
If:
the ACCC has given a notice under section 151W revoking a joint functional separation undertaking; and
the revocation has not taken effect;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to each of the persons who gave the undertaking, vary the undertaking.
The ACCC must not vary a joint functional separation undertaking under subsection (3) unless the variation:
addresses the matter or matters that constituted the grounds for the revocation of the undertaking under section 151W; and
does not address any other matter.
When variation takes effect
A variation under subsection (1) or (3) takes effect at the time the notice is given.

section.heading: Reporting obligations following giving of revocation notice

content.p: Standard functional separation undertaking
If:
the ACCC has given a notice under section 151W revoking a standard functional separation undertaking; and
the revocation has not taken effect;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to the person who gave the undertaking, direct the person:
to give the ACCC:
a report about the person’s compliance with the undertaking; or
information about the person’s compliance with the undertaking; or
a report about action that the person has taken, is taking, or proposes to take for the purpose of ensuring that the person complies with sections 142C and 143 after the revocation takes effect; or

information about action that the person has taken, is taking, or proposes to take for the purpose of ensuring that the person complies with sections 142C and 143 after the revocation takes effect; and
to do so within the period specified in the direction.
Note: See section 151ZJ (self-incrimination).
Joint functional separation undertaking
If:
the ACCC has given a notice under section 151W revoking a joint functional separation undertaking; and
the revocation has not taken effect;
the ACCC may, by written notice given to a person who gave the undertaking jointly with one or more other persons, direct the person:
to give the ACCC:
a report about the person’s compliance with the undertaking; or
information about the person’s compliance with the undertaking; or
a report about action that the person has taken, is taking, or proposes to take for the purpose of ensuring that the person complies with sections 142C and 143 after the revocation takes effect; or

information about action that the person has taken, is taking, or proposes to take for the purpose of ensuring that the person complies with sections 142C and 143 after the revocation takes effect; and
to do so within the period specified in the direction.
Note: See section 151ZJ (self-incrimination).
Compliance with direction
A person must comply with a direction under subsection (1) or (2).
Ancillary contraventions
A person must not:
aid, abet, counsel or procure a contravention of subsection (3); or
induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a contravention of subsection (3); or
be in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, a contravention of subsection (3); or
conspire with others to effect a contravention of subsection (3).
Civil penalty provisions
(5) Subsections (3) and (4) are civil penalty provisions.
Note: Part 31 provides for pecuniary penalties for breaches of civil penalty provisions.

section.heading: Requirement to notify changes in control of person who gave undertaking

content.p: Notification by person who gave undertaking
If:
(a) a functional separation undertaking given by a person (the first person) is in force; and
the first person becomes aware that:
a person who was not in a position to exercise control of the first person has become in a position to exercise control of the first person; or
a person who was in a position to control the first person has ceased to be in that position;
the first person must:
notify the ACCC, in writing, of that event; and
do so as soon as practicable, but not later than 10 business days, after becoming so aware.
Note: See section 154.
The notice must be in a form approved, in writing, by the ACCC.
Notification by controller of person who gave undertaking
If:
(a) a functional separation undertaking given by a person (the first person) is in force; and
another person becomes aware that the other person is in a position to exercise control of the first person;
the other person must:
notify the ACCC, in writing, of that position; and
do so as soon as practicable, but not later than 10 business days, after becoming so aware.
Note: See section 154.
The notice must be in a form approved, in writing, by the ACCC.
Ancillary contraventions
A person must not:
aid, abet, counsel or procure a contravention of subsection (1) or (3); or
induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a contravention of subsection (1) or (3); or
be in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, a contravention of subsection (1) or (3); or
conspire with others to effect a contravention of subsection (1) or (3).
Civil penalty provisions
(6) Subsections (1), (3) and (5) are civil penalty provisions.
Note: Part 31 provides for pecuniary penalties for breaches of civil penalty provisions.
The ACCC is to maintain a Register in which the ACCC includes:
all functional separation undertakings that have been accepted by the ACCC (including those that are no longer in force); and
in the case of a functional separation undertaking that, under section 151B, is taken to have been given by a corporation:
the name of the corporation; and
the date the undertaking came into force; and
all variations of functional separation undertakings.
The Register is to be maintained by electronic means.
The Register is to be made available for inspection on the ACCC’s website.
The Register is not a legislative instrument.
If a functional separation undertaking given by a person is in force, the person must comply with the undertaking.
Note: See also section 142B.
Ancillary contraventions
A person must not:
aid, abet, counsel or procure a contravention of subsection (1); or
induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a contravention of subsection (1); or
be in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, a contravention of subsection (1); or
conspire with others to effect a contravention of subsection (1).
Civil penalty provisions
(3) Subsections (1) and (2) are civil penalty provisions.
Note: Part 31 provides for pecuniary penalties for breaches of civil penalty provisions.
If:
a functional separation undertaking given by a person is in force; and
the Federal Court is satisfied, on the application of:
the ACCC; or
a carrier; or
a carriage service provider;
that the person has breached the undertaking;
the Court may make any or all of the following orders:
an order directing the person to comply with the undertaking;
an order directing the disposal of network units, lines, shares or other assets;
an order restraining the exercise of any rights attached to shares;
an order prohibiting or deferring the payment of any sums due to a person in respect of shares held by the person;
an order that any exercise of rights attached to shares be disregarded;

an order directing the person to pay to the Commonwealth an amount up to the amount of any financial benefit that the person has obtained directly or indirectly and that is reasonably attributable to the breach;
any order that the Court considers appropriate directing the person to compensate any other person (who may be the applicant) who has suffered loss or damage as a result of the breach;
any other order that the Court considers appropriate.
Note: See also section 142B.
In addition to the Federal Court’s powers under subsection (1), the Court:
has power, for the purpose of securing compliance with any other order made under this section, to make an order directing any person to do, or refrain from doing, a specified act; and
has power to make an order containing such ancillary or consequential provisions as the Court thinks just.

The Federal Court may, before making an order under this section, direct that notice of the application be given to such persons as it thinks fit or be published in such manner as it thinks fit, or both.
The Federal Court may, by order, rescind, vary or discharge an order made by it under this section or suspend the operation of such an order.

section.heading: Eligible services to be supplied on a non-discriminatory basis

content.p: No discrimination between wholesale customers
If:
an eligible service is supplied, or proposed to be supplied, by a person using a local access line; and
any of the following conditions is satisfied:
section 142C applies to the line;
section 143 applies to the line;

neither section 142C nor section 143 applies to the line, and there is in force a functional separation undertaking that relates to local access line services supplied, or proposed to be supplied, using the line;

the person must not, on or after the designated commencement date, discriminate between the person’s wholesale customers, or the person’s prospective wholesale customers, in relation to the supply of eligible services using the line.

The rule in subsection (1) does not prevent discrimination against a wholesale customer, or prospective wholesale customer, if the person has reasonable grounds to believe that the wholesale customer or prospective wholesale customer would fail, to a material extent, to comply with the terms and conditions on which the person supplies eligible services using the line.
Examples of grounds for believing as mentioned in subsection (2) include:
evidence that the wholesale customer or prospective wholesale customer is not creditworthy; and
repeated failures by the wholesale customer or prospective wholesale customer to comply with the terms and conditions on which the person supplied eligible services (whether or not using the line).
No discrimination by a person in favour of itself
If:
a person supplies, or proposes to supply, an eligible service using a local access line:
to itself; and
to its wholesale customers or prospective wholesale customers; and
any of the following conditions is satisfied:
section 142C applies to the line;
section 143 applies to the line;

neither section 142C nor section 143 applies to the line, and there is in force a functional separation undertaking that relates to local access line services supplied, or proposed to be supplied, using the line;
the person must not, on or after the designated commencement date, discriminate in favour of itself in relation to the supply of the eligible service.
Ancillary contraventions
A person must not:
aid, abet, counsel or procure a contravention of subsection (1) or (4); or
induce, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, a contravention of subsection (1) or (4); or
be in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, a contravention of subsection (1) or (4); or
conspire with others to effect a contravention of subsection (1) or (4).
Civil penalty provisions
(6) Subsections (1), (4) and (5) are civil penalty provisions.
Note: Part 31 provides for pecuniary penalties for breaches of civil penalty provisions.

section.heading: Eligible services—related activities to be carried on on a non-discriminatory basis

content.p: Scope
This section applies to a person, on and after the designated commencement date, if:
an eligible service is supplied, or proposed to be supplied, by a person using a local access line; and
any of the following conditions is satisfied:
section 142C applies to the line;
section 143 applies to the line;

neither section 142C nor section 143 applies to the line, and there is in force a functional separation undertaking that relates to local access line services supplied, or proposed to be supplied, using the line.
No discrimination between wholesale customers
The person must not, in carrying on any of the following activities, discriminate between the person’s wholesale customers or the person’s prospective wholesale customers:
developing a new eligible service;
enhancing an eligible service;
extending or enhancing the capability of a facility or telecommunications network by means of which an eligible service is, or is to be, supplied;
planning for a facility or telecommunications network by means of which an eligible service is, or is to be, supplied;
an activity that is preparatory to the supply of an eligible service;
an activity that is ancillary or incidental to the supply of an eligible service;
giving information to service providers about any of the above activities.
No discrimination by a person in favour of itself
The person must not discriminate in favour of itself in relation to the carrying on of any of the following activities:
developing a new eligible service;
enhancing an eligible service;

section.heading: Review by the Australian Competition Tribunal

content.p: If the ACCC makes a decision under section 151F to reject a functional separation undertaking that was given by a person or persons, the person or persons may apply to the Australian Competition Tribunal for a review of the decision.

If the ACCC makes a decision under section 151N to vary a functional separation undertaking that was given by a person or persons, the person or persons may apply to the Australian Competition Tribunal for a review of the decision.

If the ACCC makes a decision under section 151T to reject a variation that was given by a person or persons, the person or persons may apply to the Australian Competition Tribunal for a review of the decision.

If the ACCC makes a decision under section 151W to revoke a functional separation undertaking that was given by a person or persons, the person or persons may apply to the Australian Competition Tribunal for a review of the decision.

If the ACCC makes a decision under section 151Z to vary a functional separation undertaking that was given by a person or persons, the person or persons may apply to the Australian Competition Tribunal for a review of the decision.
An application under this section for a review of a decision must be:
in writing; and
in the case of an application under subsection (1), (3), (4) or (5)—made within 21 days after the ACCC made the decision; and
in the case of an application under subsection (2)—made within 14 days after the ACCC made the decision.
If the Australian Competition Tribunal receives an application under this section for a review of a decision, the Australian Competition Tribunal must review the decision.

section.heading: Functions and powers of the Australian Competition Tribunal etc.

content.p: Decision on review
On a review of a decision of the ACCC of a kind mentioned in section 151ZL, the Australian Competition Tribunal may make a decision:
affirming the ACCC’s decision; or
setting aside the ACCC’s decision;
and, for the purposes of the review, the Australian Competition Tribunal may perform all the functions and exercise all the powers of the ACCC.
A decision by the Australian Competition Tribunal:
affirming a decision of the ACCC; or
setting aside a decision of the ACCC;
is taken, for the purposes of this Act (other than this section or section 151ZL), to be a decision of the ACCC.

division.heading: Service areas and statutory infrastructure providers

content.p: Subdivision AA—Introduction
• There are 4 types of service area, as follows:
an interim NBN service area;
the general service area;
a nominated service area;
a designated service area.
• Interim NBN service areas exist only before the designated day.
• The general service area exists only after the start of the designated day.
• An NBN corporation will be the statutory infrastructure provider for an interim NBN service area.
• NBN Co will be the statutory infrastructure provider for the general service area.
• A nominated service area is an area that is attributable to:
a declaration made by a carrier; or
certain carrier licence conditions declarations made by the Minister.
• The statutory infrastructure provider for a nominated service area that is attributable to a declaration made by a carrier will be:
the carrier; or
another carrier declared by the Minister.
• The statutory infrastructure provider for a nominated service area that is attributable to a carrier licence conditions declaration will be:
the carrier to whom the carrier licence conditions declaration applies; or
another carrier declared by the Minister.
• A designated service area is an area declared by the Minister.
• The statutory infrastructure provider for a designated service area will be a carrier declared by the Minister.
• Nominated service areas and designated service areas are excluded from interim NBN service areas and the general service area.
• Designated service areas are excluded from nominated service areas.
For the purposes of this Part, service area means:
before the designated day:
an interim NBN service area; or
a nominated service area; or
a designated service area; or
after the start of the designated day:
the general service area; or
a nominated service area; or
a designated service area.

the whole or a part of a nominated service area; or
the whole or a part of a designated service area.

If, during the period:

ending immediately before the designated day;

(c) by written instrument, declare that the area is a provisional interim NBN service area for the purposes of the application of this Part before the designated day; and
do so within 10 business days after the end of the month in which the statement began to be published.
Note: For the format of the description of the area, see section 360LA.
If, before the commencement of this section, there was published on NBN Co’s website a statement to the effect that a particular area in Australia is ready for service, NBN Co must:
(a) by written instrument, declare that the area is a provisional interim NBN service area for the purposes of the application of this Part before the designated day; and

Note: For the format of the description of the area, see section 360LA.

NBN Co must publish a copy of a declaration made by it under subsection (2) or (3) on its website.
NBN Co must give a copy of a declaration made by it under subsection (2) or (3) to the ACMA.

A declaration made under subsection (2) or (3) cannot be revoked.
Variation

section.heading: Obligation of statutory infrastructure provider to connect premises

content.p: The statutory infrastructure provider for a service area must, on reasonable request by a carriage service provider on behalf of an end-user at premises in the service area:

connect the premises to a qualifying fixed-line telecommunications network in order that the carriage service provider can provide qualifying fixed-line carriage services to the end-user at the premises; or

if it is not reasonable for the statutory infrastructure provider to connect the premises to a qualifying fixed-line telecommunications network—connect the premises to a qualifying telecommunications network in order that the carriage service provider can provide:
qualifying fixed wireless carriage services to the end-user at the premises; or
qualifying satellite carriage services to the end-user at the premises.
Exceptions
An obligation does not arise under subsection (1) in relation to the connection of premises in the circumstances (if any) specified in a determination under subsection (3).
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine circumstances for the purposes of subsection (2).
Requirements
In fulfilling its obligations under subsection (1), the statutory infrastructure provider for a service area must comply with such requirements (if any) as are determined under subsection (5).
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine one or more requirements for the purposes of subsection (4).
A requirement may be of general application or may be limited to one or more service areas.
(7) Subsection (6) does not, by implication, limit the application of subsection 33(3A) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
Terms and conditions
If:
a carriage service provider makes a request as mentioned in subsection (1) in relation to the connection of premises in a service area; and
as a result, the statutory infrastructure provider has an obligation under subsection (1) to connect the premises; and
the statutory infrastructure provider has published on its website:
the terms and conditions relating to price or a method of ascertaining price; and
other terms and conditions;

on which it offers to connect premises in the service area to a qualifying telecommunications network in order that a carriage service provider can provide qualifying carriage services to an end-user at the premises; and
the carriage service provider requests the statutory infrastructure provider to enter into an agreement that:

relates to the connection of premises in the service area to a qualifying telecommunications network in order that the carriage service provider can provide qualifying carriage services to an end-user at the premises; and
sets out terms and conditions that are the same as the terms and conditions published as mentioned in paragraph (c);
the statutory infrastructure provider must comply with the request mentioned in paragraph (d).

a carriage service provider makes a request as mentioned in subsection (1) in relation to the connection of premises; and
as a result, the statutory infrastructure provider has an obligation under subsection (1) to connect the premises; and
the connection is not covered by an agreement between the statutory infrastructure provider and the carriage service provider;

the statutory infrastructure provider must comply with the obligation on the terms and conditions that were published on the statutory infrastructure provider’s website at the time when the request was made.
Note: For publication, see section 360W.

The Minister may, by legislative instrument:

determine that, if the condition specified in the determination is satisfied in relation to premises, then, for the purposes of subsection (1), it is taken not to be reasonable for a statutory infrastructure provider to connect the premises to a qualifying fixed-line telecommunications network; or

determine that, if the conditions specified in the determination are satisfied in relation to premises, then, for the purposes of subsection (1), it is taken not to be reasonable for a statutory infrastructure provider to connect the premises to a qualifying fixed-line telecommunications network.
A determination under subsection (10) must be an instrument of a legislative character.
Response to request
If a carriage service provider makes a request as mentioned in subsection (1) on behalf of an end-user at particular premises:
the statutory infrastructure provider must:
notify the carriage service provider that the statutory infrastructure provider will fulfil the request; or
refuse the request; and
do so within:
10 business days after receiving the request; or
if a longer period is specified under subsection (11B)—that longer period.

a carriage service provider makes a request as mentioned in subsection (1) on behalf of an end-user at particular premises; and
the statutory infrastructure provider refuses the request;
then:
the statutory infrastructure provider must:
give written notice of the refusal to the carriage service provider; and
do so within 5 business days after the refusal; and
if the carriage service provider receives the notice—the carriage service provider must:
give a copy of the notice to the end-user; and
do so within 5 business days after receiving the notice.

section.heading: Obligation of statutory infrastructure provider to supply eligible services—premises

content.p: The statutory infrastructure provider for a service area must, on reasonable request by a carriage service provider:
supply an eligible service to the carriage service provider in order that the carriage service provider can provide qualifying carriage services to end-users at premises in the service area; and
do so on the terms and conditions that were published on the statutory infrastructure provider’s website at the time when the request was made.
Note: For publication, see section 360X.

The eligible service must enable the carriage service provider to supply, to end-users at premises in the service area, carriage services that can be used by those end-users to make and receive voice calls.
Subsection (1A) does not apply if the carriage service is supplied using a satellite.
To avoid doubt, the requirement in subsection (1A) is part of the obligation under subsection (1).
Exceptions
If:

a statutory infrastructure provider for a service area supplies an eligible service to a carriage service provider in order that the carriage service provider can provide qualifying carriage services to end-users at premises in the service area; and

the eligible service enables the carriage service provider to supply, to end-users at premises in the service area, carriage services that can be used by those end-users to make and receive voice calls; and
(c) the eligible service is a declared service (within the meaning of Part XIC of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010); and
(d) the statutory infrastructure provider is subject to a standard access obligation (within the meaning of Part XIC of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010) in relation to the eligible service;

the statutory infrastructure provider does not have an obligation under subsection (1) to supply the eligible service to the carriage service provider in order that the carriage service provider can provide qualifying carriage services to end-users at premises in the service area.
Paragraph (2)(b) does not apply if the carriage service is supplied using a satellite.
An obligation does not arise under subsection (1) in relation to supply of an eligible service in the circumstances (if any) specified in a determination under subsection (4).
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine circumstances for the purposes of subsection (3).
Requirements
In fulfilling its obligations under subsection (1), the statutory infrastructure provider for a service area must comply with such requirements (if any) as are determined under subsection (6).
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine one or more requirements for the purposes of subsection (5).
A requirement may be of general application or may be limited to one or more service areas.
(8) Subsection (7) does not, by implication, limit the application of subsection 33(3A) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.

If:
a carriage service provider makes a request as mentioned in subsection (1) in relation to the supply of an eligible service; and
as a result, the statutory infrastructure provider has an obligation under subsection (1) to supply the eligible service; and
the statutory infrastructure provider has published on its website:
the terms and conditions relating to price or a method of ascertaining price; and
other terms and conditions;

on which it offers to supply eligible services to carriage service providers in order that the carriage service providers can provide qualifying carriage services to end-users at premises in the service area; and
the carriage service provider requests the statutory infrastructure provider to enter into an agreement that:

relates to the supply of eligible services to the carriage service provider in order that the carriage service provider can provide qualifying carriage services to end-users at premises in the service area; and
sets out terms and conditions that are the same as the terms and conditions published as mentioned in paragraph (c);
the statutory infrastructure provider must comply with the request mentioned in paragraph (d).
Note: For publication, see section 360X.
If:
a carriage service provider makes a request as mentioned in subsection (1) in relation to the supply of an eligible service; and
as a result, the statutory infrastructure provider has an obligation under subsection (1) to supply the eligible service; and
the supply of the eligible service is not covered by an agreement between the statutory infrastructure provider and the carriage service provider;

the statutory infrastructure provider must comply with the obligation on the terms and conditions that were published on the statutory infrastructure provider’s website at the time when the request was made.
Note: For publication, see section 360X.

content.p: A statutory infrastructure provider for a service area must publish on its website:

division.heading: Chargeable premises associated with a local access line

section.heading: Chargeable premises associated with a local access line

content.p: For the purposes of this Part, if:
a person is a carrier; and
particular premises are potentially chargeable premises in relation to the person for a month; and
the premises are not exempt premises in relation to the person for the month;
the premises are chargeable premises associated with a local access line of the person for the month.
If:
a person is a carrier; and
during a period comprising the whole or a part of a month in an eligible financial year, either:
the person owns a local access line, but no nominated carrier declaration is in force in relation to the line; or
under a nominated carrier declaration, the person is the nominated carrier in relation to a local access line; and
the line is not an exempt line in relation to the person for the month; and
during the whole or a part of the period, a carriage service provider (who may be the person) supplies a designated broadband service to particular premises in Australia using the line;
the premises are potentially chargeable premises in relation to the person for the month.

Note: The line does not need to be physically connected to the premises. This is because using has an extended meaning—see subsection 5(1) of this Act and section 24 of the Telecommunications Act 1997 (when read together with section 18A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901).
If:
a person is a member of an associated group during the whole or a part of a month; and
the total number of potentially chargeable premises in relation to the members of the group for that month is less than 2,000; and
one or more of those potentially chargeable premises are potentially chargeable premises in relation to the person for that month;
each of the potentially chargeable premises mentioned in paragraph (c) are exempt premises in relation to the person for that month.
If:
a person is not a member of an associated group during the whole or a part of a month; and
the total number of potentially chargeable premises in relation to the person for that month is less than 2,000;
each of those potentially chargeable premises are exempt premises in relation to the person for that month.
Associated group
For the purposes of this section, if:
a person is in a position to exercise control of:
a local access line; or
a telecommunications network; and
the person has one or more associates;
then:
the person is taken to belong to an associated group; and
the associated group consists of the person and those associates.
For the purposes of subsection (3), the question of whether a person is in a position to exercise control of:
a local access line; or
a telecommunications network;
is to be determined in the same manner in which that question is determined for the purposes of Part 8 of the Telecommunications Act 1997.

(5) For the purposes of subsection (3), the question of whether a person has one or more associates is to be determined in the same manner in which that question is determined for the purposes of Part 8 of the Telecommunications Act 1997.

content.p: Telstra

a person is a carrier; and
during a period comprising the whole or a part of a month in an eligible financial year, either:
the person owns a local access line, but there is no nominated carrier declaration in force in relation to the line; or

the line is not owned by an NBN corporation at any time during that month; and
the line is not used by an NBN corporation to supply a declared service at any time during that month; and
during the whole of that month, there was in force a legally enforceable agreement that satisfies the following conditions:
the agreement provides for the transfer of ownership or control of the line to an NBN corporation;

Optus
If:
a person is a carrier; and
during a period comprising the whole or a part of a month in an eligible financial year, either:
the person owns a local access line, but there is no nominated carrier declaration in force in relation to the line; or
under a nominated carrier declaration, the person is the nominated carrier in relation to a local access line; and
the line is not owned by an NBN corporation at any time during that month; and
the line is not used by an NBN corporation to supply a declared service at any time during that month; and

the line is an exempt line in relation to the person for that month.

Other networks
If:
a person is a carrier; and
during a period comprising the whole or a part of a month in an eligible financial year, either:
the person owns a local access line, but there is no nominated carrier declaration in force in relation to the line; or
under a nominated carrier declaration, the person is the nominated carrier in relation to a local access line; and
that month is one of the first 6 months of the first eligible financial year; and

during the whole of that month, there was in force a legally enforceable agreement that satisfies the following conditions:

the agreement was in force immediately before the commencement of this section;
the agreement is not covered by subparagraph (1)(e)(ii) or (3)(e)(ii);
the agreement is not specified in an instrument under subsection (6);
such other conditions (if any) as are determined under subsection (7);
the line is an exempt line in relation to the person for that month.
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, specify one or more agreements for the purposes of subparagraph (5)(f)(iv).
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine one or more conditions for the purposes of subparagraph (5)(f)(v).
When agreement comes into force
For the purposes of this section, an agreement is taken to come into force when the agreement is entered into.

For the purposes of this Part, if particular premises are potentially chargeable premises in relation to a person for a month because a carriage service provider (who may be the person) supplies a designated broadband service to:
a residential customer who occupies the premises; or

the premises are potentially concessional premises in relation to the person for that month.
If:
during a period comprising the whole or a part of a month in an eligible financial year, a person is a carrier; and
(b) a declaration made under subsection 63(2) of the Telecommunications Act 1997 was in force on 30 June 2018 in relation to the carrier licence held by the person; and

the declaration provides that the person must (upon request by an end-user at relevant premises) connect, or arrange for another person on the person’s behalf to connect, premises located in a development area (however described) specified in the declaration to a telecommunications network owned by the person (as specified in the declaration); and

If:

during a period comprising the whole or a part of a month in an eligible financial year, the person supplies an eligible local bitstream access service using a local access line; and

was made:

Civil penalty provisions
(3) Subsections (1), (1A) and (2) are civil penalty provisions.
Note: Part 31 of the Telecommunications Act 1997 provides for pecuniary penalties for breaches of civil penalty provisions.
Offences
A carrier commits an offence if:
the carrier, either alone or together with one or more other persons, enters into, begins to carry out or carries out a scheme; and
the carrier did so for the sole or dominant purpose of avoiding the application of:
section 93 of this Act; or
(ii) any provision of the Telecommunications (Regional Broadband Scheme) Charge Act 2020 (other than section 20 of that Act);
in relation to:

Scheme
(6) For the purposes of this section, scheme means:
any agreement, arrangement, understanding, promise or undertaking, whether express or implied; or

Application
If:
a person is an eligible funding recipient; and
(b) the ACMA has made an assessment under section 102 setting out the charge payable by the person for a financial year (the charge financial year);
the person may, at any time during the period:
beginning when the assessment was made; and
ending at the end of the standard due date (within the meaning of section 102D) for the charge financial year;
apply to the Secretary for the issue to the person of a charge offset certificate for the charge financial year.
An application under subsection (1) must:
be in writing; and
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Secretary; and
be accompanied by such information as is specified in rules made under subsection (9).
Issue of certificate
If:
an application under subsection (1) has been made for the issue to a person of a charge offset certificate for the charge financial year; and
the person is the holder of a nominal funding entitlement certificate in relation to the next financial year; and
rules made under subsection (9) for the purposes of this paragraph are in force; and
the conditions set out in those rules are satisfied;
the Secretary must:
issue a certificate stating that the person is entitled to a charge offset for the charge financial year equal to the amount specified in the certificate; and
do so by the end of 31 March next following the charge financial year.
The amount specified in the certificate:
must be the amount ascertained in accordance with rules made under subsection (9); and
must not exceed the nominal funding entitlement of the person for the next financial year; and
must not exceed the annual base amount of the person for the charge financial year.
(5) A certificate issued under subsection (3) is to be known as a charge offset certificate.
Refusal
If the Secretary decides to refuse to issue a charge offset certificate to a person, the Secretary must give written notice of the decision to the person.
Copy of certificate
If the Secretary issues a charge offset certificate, the Secretary must give a copy of the certificate to the ACMA.
Charge offset certificate cannot be transferred
A charge offset certificate cannot be transferred.
Rules
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make rules for the purposes of this section.
Remission
If:
a person becomes the holder of a charge offset certificate for a financial year; and
a base instalment of charge is payable by the person in relation to the financial year; and
the base instalment of charge has not been paid;
the Secretary must, on behalf of the Commonwealth, remit so much of the base instalment of charge as equals the amount specified in the certificate.
Note: For base instalment of charge, see section 102D.

If:
the ACMA has made an assessment under section 102 setting out the charge payable by a person for a financial year; and
the base instalment of charge is remitted, to any extent, under subsection (1) of this section; and
the ACMA is informed of the remission;
the ACMA must, under subsection 102B(1), vary the assessment to reflect the remission.
Refund
If:
a person becomes the holder of a charge offset certificate for a financial year; and
a base instalment of charge was payable by the person in relation to the financial year; and
the base instalment of charge has been paid;
the Secretary must, on behalf of the Commonwealth, refund so much of the base instalment of charge as equals the amount specified in the certificate.
Note: For base instalment of charge, see section 102D.

division.heading: Assessment, collection and recovery of charge

content.p: Subdivision A—Reporting obligations
If there are one or more chargeable premises associated with a local access line of a person for a month in an eligible financial year, the person must:
give the ACMA a written report about:
those chargeable premises; and
the chargeable premises (if any) associated with a local access line of the person for each of the other months in the financial year; and
do so before the end of 31 October next following the financial year.
The report must be in a form approved, in writing, by the ACMA.
The approved form may require verification, by a statutory declaration, of statements made in the report.
If, at any time during a month covered by the report, the person had an associate in relation to control of:
a telecommunications network; or
a company; or
a local access line;
the report must:
set out the name of the associate; and
set out the ACN (if any) of the associate; and
identify the network, company or line, as the case requires; and
(g) identify which paragraph or paragraphs of subsection 152(1) of the Telecommunications Act 1997 resulted in the person having the associate.
Transitional
If:
the report relates to:
the first eligible financial year; or
the second eligible financial year; or
the third eligible financial year; or
the fourth eligible financial year; or
the fifth eligible financial year; and
there are one or more potentially concessional premises in relation to the person for a month in the eligible financial year;
the report must set out the total number of potentially concessional premises in relation to the person for that month.
If:
particular premises are reported as potentially concessional premises in relation to the person for a month; and
apart from this subsection, the premises are not potentially concessional premises in relation to the person for the month; and
the person:
did not know; and
could not, with reasonable diligence, have ascertained;
that the premises are not potentially concessional premises in relation to the person for the month;
the premises are taken, for all purposes, to be potentially concessional premises in relation to the person for the month.
If:
the report relates to:
the first eligible financial year; or
the second eligible financial year; or
the third eligible financial year; or
the fourth eligible financial year; or
the fifth eligible financial year; and
during the whole or a part of a month in the eligible financial year, the person was the controller of an associated group;
the report must:
set out a statement to that effect; and
identify each of the members of the associated group; and
set out the circumstances that resulted in the person being the controller of the associated group.
Associated group
For the purposes of subsection (6), if:
a person is in a position to exercise control of:
a local access line; or
a telecommunications network; and
the person has one or more associates;
then:
the person is taken to belong to an associated group; and
the associated group consists of the person and those associates; and
the person is the controller of the associated group.
For the purposes of subsection (7), the question of whether a person is in a position to exercise control of:
a local access line; or
a telecommunications network;
is to be determined in the same manner in which that question is determined for the purposes of Part 8 of the Telecommunications Act 1997.

(9) For the purposes of subsection (7), the question of whether a person has one or more associates is to be determined in the same manner in which that question is determined for the purposes of Part 8 of the Telecommunications Act 1997.
Transitional—recently connected greenfield premises
If:
the report relates to:
the first eligible financial year; or
the second eligible financial year; or
the third eligible financial year; or
the fourth eligible financial year; or
the fifth eligible financial year; and
there are one or more recently connected greenfield premises in relation to the person for a month in the eligible financial year;
the report must set out the total number of recently connected greenfield premises in relation to the person for that month.
If:
particular premises are reported as recently connected greenfield premises in relation to the person for a month; and
apart from this subsection, the premises are not recently connected greenfield premises in relation to the person for the month; and
the person:
did not know; and
could not, with reasonable diligence, have ascertained;
that the premises are not recently connected greenfield premises in relation to the person for the month;
the premises are taken, for all purposes, to be recently connected greenfield premises in relation to the person for the month.

section.heading: Offence of failing to lodge report

content.p: A person commits a strict liability offence if:
the person is subject to a requirement under section 100; and
the person omits to do an act; and
the omission breaches the requirement.
Penalty: 50 penalty units.
A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits a separate offence in respect of each day (including a day of a conviction for the offence or any later day) during which the contravention continues.
Subdivision B—Assessments
If a person has given the ACMA a section 100 report in relation to a financial year before the end of 31 October next following the financial year, the ACMA must:
make a written assessment setting out:
the total number of chargeable premises (if any) associated with a local access line of the person for each of the months in the financial year; and
the person’s annual chargeable premises amount (if any) for the financial year; and
the person’s annual base amount (if any) for the financial year; and
the person’s annual administrative cost amount (if any) for the financial year; and
the charge (if any) payable by the person in relation to the financial year; and
do so by the assessment deadline for the financial year.
Note 1: Section 102D sets out when the charge is payable.
Note 2: If a month is in the first, second, third, fourth of fifth eligible financial year, the total number mentioned in paragraph (a) may be reduced—see subsection (6).

If a person has not given the ACMA a section 100 report in relation to a financial year before the end of 31 October next following the financial year, the ACMA may, before the assessment deadline for the financial year, make a written assessment setting out:
the total number of chargeable premises (if any) associated with a local access line of the person for each of the months in the financial year; and
the person’s annual chargeable premises amount (if any) for the financial year; and
the person’s annual base amount (if any) for the financial year; and
the person’s annual administrative cost amount (if any) for the financial year; and
the charge (if any) payable by the person in relation to the financial year.
Note 1: Section 102D sets out when the charge is payable.
Note 2: If a month is in the first, second, third, fourth of fifth eligible financial year, the total number mentioned in paragraph (a) may be reduced—see subsection (6).
An assessment under this section is not a legislative instrument.
Assessment deadline
(4) For the purposes of this section, the assessment deadline for a financial year is the end of:
30 November next following the financial year; or
if:
a later day is ascertained in accordance with a determination made under subsection (5); and
the day ascertained in accordance with the determination is not later than 2 months before the standard due date (within the meaning of section 102D) for the financial year;
the day ascertained in accordance with the determination.
The ACMA may, by legislative instrument, make a determination for the purposes of subparagraph (4)(b)(i).

As soon as practicable after making an assessment under section 102, the ACMA must give a copy of the assessment to:
the person to whom the assessment relates; and

The ACMA may vary an assessment made under this Division by making such alterations and additions as it thinks necessary, even if charge has been paid in respect of an assessment.
Unless the contrary intention appears, a varied assessment is taken, for the purposes of this Division, to be an assessment under section 102.
Despite anything in this Division, the ACMA may, for the purposes of making an assessment under this Division, partly or completely accept a statement in a report under section 100.
Subdivision C—Collection and recovery of charge
Person other than an eligible funding recipient
Charge payable by a person (other than an eligible funding recipient) in relation to a financial year becomes due and payable on:
the standard due date for the financial year; or
if the ACMA, by written notice given to the person, allows a later day—that later day.
A day allowed under paragraph (1)(b) must not be later than 28 February next following the financial year.
A copy of a notice under paragraph (1)(b) must be published on the ACMA’s website.
A notice under paragraph (1)(b) is not a legislative instrument.
Eligible funding recipient
If a person is an eligible funding recipient, charge payable by the person in relation to a financial year is payable in 2 instalments, as follows:
(a) an instalment (the base instalment) of so much of the amount of the charge as equals the annual base amount of the person for the financial year;
(b) an instalment (the administrative cost instalment) of so much of the amount of the charge as equals the annual administrative cost amount of the person for the financial year.
If a person is an eligible funding recipient, the base instalment of charge payable by the person in relation to a financial year becomes due and payable on:
if the person has made an application under subsection 98(1) for a charge offset certificate for the financial year—30 April next following the financial year; or
otherwise:
the standard due date for the financial year; or
if the ACMA, by written notice given to the person, allows a later day—that later day.
A day allowed under subparagraph (6)(b)(ii) must not be later than 28 February next following the financial year.

section.heading: Report about the number of premises supplied with designated broadband services during the applicable reporting period

content.p: Reportable premises
For the purposes of this section, if:

the person owns a local access line, but there is no nominated carrier declaration in force in relation to the line; or
under a nominated carrier declaration, the person is the nominated carrier in relation to a local access line; and
during the whole or a part of the period, a carriage service provider (who may be the person) supplies a designated broadband service to particular premises in Australia using the line;
the premises are reportable premises in relation to the person for the applicable reporting period.

a person is a carrier; and
